slides.title: Mold and contaminants
slides.body: Inspectors don't have to look for mold, toxins, or soil, water or air contaminants. Ask about separate testing.
slides.source: N.J.A.C. 13:40-15.16, NJ home inspection standards (accessed Oct. 2026)

slides.title: Underground fuel tanks
slides.body: The fuel tank part of the inspection leaves out underground storage tanks. Ask about a separate tank sweep.
slides.source: N.J.A.C. 13:40-15.16, NJ home inspection standards (accessed Oct. 2026)

slides.title: Well water
slides.body: Wells, well pumps and water quality or quantity are left out. If the home has a well, ask about a water test.
slides.source: N.J.A.C. 13:40-15.16, NJ home inspection standards (accessed Oct. 2026)

slides.title: Code checks and repair prices
slides.body: Inspectors don't have to check code compliance or price out repairs. Get contractor quotes. Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.

caption:
Nobody wants to admit this, but your NJ home inspection can skip things. NJ's home inspection rules list what the inspector doesn't have to check.

Here are 4 of them:
1. Mold, toxins, and soil, water or air contaminants.
2. Underground fuel storage tanks. Ask about a separate tank sweep.
3. Wells, well pumps and water quality. If the home has a well, ask about a water test.
4. Code compliance and the cost of repairs. Get contractor quotes.

Read your inspection agreement so you know what's covered before inspection day.

Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.
